problem: If the $15$th term of an arithmetic series is $-53$ and the sum of the first $21$ terms is $-777,$ then the first term of the series is ${a}_{1}=${{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
We are given one term of the series. So, to find the first term, we use the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series in the form

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d),
$$

where ${a}_{1}$ is the first term, $d$ is the common difference, and $N$ is the number of terms.

Substituting $N=21$ and ${S}_{N}=-777$ into the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d) \\ -777 & =\frac{21}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(21-1)d) \\ -1\,554= & 21(2{a}_{1}+20d) \\ -74 & =2{a}_{1}+20d.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, we can write an equation for the $15$th term of the arithmetic series and substitute in its known value:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\ {a}_{15} & ={a}_{1}+(15-1)d \\ -53 & ={a}_{1}+14d\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-53={a}_{1}+14d \\ -74=2{a}_{1}+20d\end{aligned}
$$

To solve this system, we multiply the first equation by $-2$ and add the result to the second equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}106 & =-2{a}_{1}-28d \\ -74 & =2{a}_{1}+20d \\ 32 & =-8d \\ d & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $d=-4$ into the first equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-53 & ={a}_{1}+14d \\ -53 & ={a}_{1}+14(-4) \\ -53 & ={a}_{1}-56 \\ {a}_{1} & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
